title: GenWave Persona Catalog Index
description: The committed index.json shape (SPEC F89.2) a GenWave station fetches directly from the repo root — built from entries/ by tools/build_index.py, and re-verified byte-for-byte plus schema-validated on every CI run (PR and push to main). additionalProperties is false throughout: this document is entirely catalog-tooling output, so an unrecognized field is a build regression worth failing CI on, not a forward-compat concern.
$comment: Every pattern below ends in (?![\s\S]), a lookahead meaning 'no character follows' — a portable absolute-end-of-string anchor that means the same thing in Python re, ECMA-262 (the dialect JSON Schema nominally specifies, and what ajv/most other validators use), and .NET. Plain $ was rejected: in Python's re (which is what actually enforces this schema server-side, via the jsonschema library), $ also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so a value with a stray trailing \n would slip through. \Z was also tried and rejected: it's Python-only — under ECMA-262, \Z is a literal 'Z' character (Annex B identity escape), so a \Z-anchored pattern would reject every legitimate value and only accept ones ending in a literal Z. (?![\s\S]) has neither problem in any of the three dialects.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD): the max `added` date across included entries' meta.json, or 1970-01-01 when the catalog has zero included entries (tools/build_index.py). Derived entirely from the tree, never from git history or wall-clock time.

entries.description: Sorted by slug. Never includes the example-dj documentation entry.

entry.description: `card`/`manifest` are conditionally required, not both listed here — see the `if`/`then`/`else` below, gated on `kind`.

kind.description: Entry discriminator (SPEC F103.2 / T178). Optional — an entry with no `kind` is treated as "persona", matching every pre-F103.2 entry and the app's own back-compat default (GenWave.Host, T176: a missing `kind` defaults to persona; an unrecognized `kind` value there causes the app to skip just that one entry, not abort the whole index — this schema is stricter than the app and rejects an unrecognized value outright, since here it can only mean a build regression in this repo's own tooling, not a newer app talking to an older catalog). `kind` decides which file-ref property below is required and which path pattern its `path` must match: "persona" (or omitted) requires `card` matching `*.persona.json` — the unchanged, pre-F103.2 shape; "theme" requires `manifest` matching `*.theme.json` — SPEC F103.2's new key, so a theme entry is never mistaken for using the legacy persona file-ref name.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<slug>/ — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out.

Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<slug>/ to the kind:"theme" manifest file (SPEC F103.2) — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out. Only present on kind:"theme" entries; persona entries keep using `card` (see the `kind` description above) rather than this key.
